text.p: Cosmetics group L'Oreal said it expected to report a sharper rise in 1996 profit before capital gains and losses, and after minority interests.
"Sales for the full year 1996 should enjoy growth close to the increase recorded for the first nine months of the year," when they rose 12.1 percent, the company said.

"Growth in profit on ordinary activities before taxation, employee profit-sharing and capital gains and losses should equal the rise in sales after allowing for the increase in the group's interest expenses," it said in a statement.

"Nineteen ninety six net profit before capital gains and losses and after minority interests should advance more strongly than in 1995 despite the increase in taxation and the portion paid to minority interests," it said.
It said in its half-year earnings statement that nine-month sales rose 12.1 percent to 44.58 billion francs. On a like-for-like basis, the rise was 7.8 percent, it said.
The difference is due mainly to the inclusion in the first half of 1996 of sales from Maybelline and Jade, two cosmetics companies acquired in the second half of 1995.
